_note: Ellen's string board (Round 2, step 5; story/FamilyStations.js; render/storyBoard.js). Every text is a draft for Aaron. items, in the order the story pins them: flag (the progress flag that pins it; null: there from the start), kind (config.familyStations.kinds), at [x, y] (its middle, metres from the board's bottom-left corner as Tom faces it), size [w, h], tilt (degrees), image (a photograph's picture, a colour), lines (ink lines on a written thing), to (where its red strings run, board coordinates), text (what Tom reads when he looks at it).

items.text: The county, out of the station's map drawer. Ellen's pins: the station, the campground, Earl's store. The south half is mostly white paper.
The four of you on the tower steps, the week you took the posting. Junie has her eyes shut.
The campers' registration card, from the station's own box. Four names. Site three. Paid up through Sunday.
A photograph of the camcorder's little screen, as near as Ellen could get it. The tents. Something tall between them that isn't a tree.
A print off camera six. A woman kneeling at the treeline in the dark, putting something in the ground.
Ellen's tally of the first night. Where they came from. How many. When they stopped. Underlined twice: THEY STOPPED AT DAWN.
Junie's drawing of the lady you saw at Earl's. A black dress, long hands, no face. Ellen pinned it up without a word.
Earl's note to Marcy, copied out in Ellen's hand. The shelter. And one line she has boxed in: do NOT go to the military checkpoint.
Ellen's transcript off Earl's scanner. Army call signs, a convoy, a checkpoint. Half the words are guesses with question marks after them.
Earl's sigils, redrawn from his tape. A ring of them round the county, every one where the dead came up. Ellen has numbered them, and crossed off the ones you've dug.
Wyatt's sketch of the thing at the treeline. 'It calls them. It shuts up when you hit it.' He has drawn cross-hairs over its head.
A page copied from Marcy Pruitt's journal. Four words of it in red: I saw it too.
One of Earl's sighting sheets, off the rack by his till. A wingspan, red eyes, a column of dates. Ellen has added today's at the bottom.
The army's field report from checkpoint seven. Loss of containment. Convoy three. Ellen has written one word in the margin: C-7?
The pilot's knee-board page. Green and purple lights, moving like nothing with wings. Ordered to force it down.
A print off the south path camera. Her torch, going away between the trees. The pin has been pushed in hard enough to bend.
The Hemlock Gap account, 1903. The voice in the trees, and the children who went to it. A hundred years to the month.
Earl's north ridge, thirty years of it. Every X a sighting. They bunch up. They always bunched up.
